answer: In PoA, each bonded identity is an accountable escrow, so splitting stake across a lotus, forge, and canyon of aliases does not dilute risk. If k coordinated identities equivocate on conflicting statements, correlated evidence triggers a quadratic aggregate penalty, O(k^2), across their escrows. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery through cheap re-registration, making sybil control economically nonviable.
